'''Maurice Carter''' (born October 12, 1976) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player.

A 6'5" [[guard (basketball)|guard]] from [[Louisiana State University]],<ref>{{cite news |author1=Jeffrey Nixon |title=The Natural |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99614020/the-natural/ |access-date=12 April 2022 |work=The Town Talk |date=14 January 1998 |page=B-3 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Dave Moormann |title=LSU's "Mo"-mentum - Carter, Tigers' lone four-year senior, bids farewell to PMAC |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99613485/lsus-mo-mentum-carter-tigers/ |access-date=12 April 2022 |work=The Town Talk |date=24 February 1999 |page=B-3 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Bruce Pascoe |title=Tough time to be a tiger |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99613210/tough-time-to-be-a-tiger/ |access-date=12 April 2022 |work=[[The Arizona Daily Star]] |date=13 February 1999 |pages=1C, 6C |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Pete McEntegart |title=Carter brings more than points to young LSU Tigers |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99613733/carter-brings-more-than-points-to-young/ |access-date=12 April 2022 |work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]] |date=8 January 1999 |page=3C |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref> Carter played ten games for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]<ref>{{cite news |author1=Tim Brown |title=Fox Steps Up; George Recedes |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-feb-02-sp-lakerep2-story.html |access-date=12 April 2022 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=2 February 2004}}</ref> and [[New Orleans Hornets]] during the [[2003-04 NBA season]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/cartema01.html Maurice Carter]. basketball-reference.</ref> He later played in [[Spain]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=esp&PlayerID=26385 Maurice Carter] at Eurobasket.</ref>

Carter played for the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) during the 2003–04 season. He was named the Finals Most Valuable Player and selected to the All-CBA Second Team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maurice Carter minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-cartemau001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=June 26, 2021}}</ref>
